_comment: The first day's gathering: hand-placed harvest spots along the tutorial path, read by scripts/world/harvest_node.gd. NOT the real M8 harvesting loop (tools, durability, the vegetation itself) — a dozen legible spots so 'gather enough to make camp' is playable today. Positions are world metres, stood on the ground per D09. ALL TUNABLE.
_comment_amounts: A camp costs 12 wood / 8 stone / 10 fiber (data/items/buildables.json), so one full walk down the practice path and back covers it with a little over: 4 wood spots x 4, 3 stone x 3, 3 fiber x 4, 2 berry x 3.
_comment_models_r9_4: R9.4. Every node here had no `model`, and harvest_node.gd's fallback for that is a BoxMesh tinted by the item's colour -- so all twelve harvest spots rendered as coloured boxes. The blind critic found two of them sitting a couple of metres from the player in the spawn framing and noted they were 'MORE legible than the player', being the only hard-edged geometric shapes in frame; it listed them among the three assets doing the most damage. These are the vegetation's own Quaternius pack, deliberately: assets/environment/nature is the Kenney kit, which ships flat untextured vertex colours including a teal-green rock material, and mixing it in would trade one cohesion problem for another (CLAUDE.md, visual cohesion). The box fallback stays in the code -- it is the right behaviour for a node whose model is missing. TUNABLE (scales especially).
